If Adam and Britt needed any confirmation they had made the right move, it came when they went to pick up a Game Boy that had been delivered to their original rental home in Hilton Head Island.
They noticed the car out front had a Colorado bumper sticker. The tenants said they had just moved from Highlands Ranch and were buying an ice cream shop with collectibles.
"They were refugees from Colorado too, and we ended up befriending them," Adam said.

Front page of a broadsheet-style newspaper, "The Pondside Picayune," No. 6, Sherman Oaks, Sunday, November 22, 2026, price one penny. Black serif type on cream paper, with thin column rules. Weather boxes flank the masthead: Sherman Oaks, clouds then light rain, 43° to 68°; Tokyo, mainly clear Monday, 39° to 56°, "one more sleep."

Lead story (World): "Education Minister Quits Over AI Exam Cheating." South Korea's education minister resigned after AI-assisted cheating on the college entrance exam; emergency phone alerts caught nearly half of 111 device cases. A right sidebar, "Ducks & Drakes" by Alpha Rae, is a whimsical household column touching on new house laws, a cat, the Tsar Bomba, and OK Computer heard in full for the first time.

Second row: "Buy, Rent Back, Retreat: A Coastal Plan," on reviving a vetoed California coastal buyout idea as El Niño tides rise; and "Chiquita Canyon: County Goes Door to Door After Gas Blast," on health workers surveying Val Verde and Castaic residents after a landfill eruption.

Third row: an "In Brief" column covering Nvidia export controls, a credit card rate cap, collapsed UN killer-robot talks, a Chico marijuana seizure, and Iran targeting a US base in Bahrain; "Weight Drugs Free Up Farmland," on a study projecting GLP-1 drugs could free land the size of Italy; and "Kinison's AI Avatar Gets a Deal," on the late comedian's estate signing with a talent agency.

Below: "Anthropic's Power Is 87% Gas, Study Says," on a nonprofit's estimate of the fuel behind Anthropic's contracted data centers; and "Founding Locks," about a lock of George Washington's hair selling at auction for $4,000.

A "Personal" strip at the bottom holds five cryptic classified-style notes addressed to The Chief, K., Bradbury, Brenda, and Sparkle.
